question: Can truly orthogonal estimators — specifically KSG (Kraskov-Stögbauer-Grassberger) conditional mutual information, Bayesian categorical model comparison (variational Bayes), or likelihood-ratio test — achieve |shuffled-action null mean| < 0.1 bits on the 12-state hash-routed SPA at N=5000, closing the estimation-bias gap that plug-in PMI (weighted/equal/median) and KNN CMI cannot?
hypothesis: H0 (null): All three orthogonal estimators have |shuffled-action null mean| >= 0.1 bits at N=5000, indicating the bias is intrinsic to plug-in estimation across strata of varying size and cannot be resolved by switching to orthogonal frameworks. H1 (alternative): At least one orthogonal estimator achieves |null_mean| < 0.1 bits, indicating the bias was specific to plug-in/KNN construction and can be eliminated by a suitable estimator. H2 (beyond-Markov, conditional on H1 passing): K3 PMI - K2 PMI > 0.1 bits with bootstrap 95% CI lower > 0.0 at N=5000 on the 12-state SPA.
falsifier: C1 (null control): All 7 estimators (4 parent + 3 orthogonal) have |shuffled-action null mean| >= 0.1 bits at N=5000. C3 (positive control): For any estimator passing C1, K3 PMI < 1.0 bit OR permutation p > 0.001 on the 8-state deterministic SPA. C6 (determinism check): Any (state, action) has < 2 unique candidates in CANDIDATES design (SPA redesign verification). C7 (size buckets): Fewer than 2 non-empty size buckets in stratum decomposition.

baselines.description: Weighted-averaged per-stratum Laplace-smoothed conditional PMI (parent null_mean=0.407)
KNN CMI estimator (k=5, alpha=1.0, parent null_mean=-0.262)
baselines.expected: null_mean may shift sign or magnitude

baselines.description: Kraskov-Stögbauer-Grassberger conditional mutual information estimator (sklearn.feature_selection.mutual_info_classif with k=5, alpha=1.0)
Bayesian categorical transition model comparison using variational Bayes (Dirichlet-Multinomial) with posterior predictive check
Likelihood-ratio test comparing full model (state+action) vs reduced model (state-only) with Bonferroni correction

positive_control: 8-state fully deterministic SPA (same as parent). Every (state, action) maps to a single next state via hash. K3 PMI should be >= 1.0 bit with p <= 0.001. This validates the estimator pipeline on a known-deterministic environment before testing on the stochastic target.
null_control: Shuffled-action null: for each of 500 permutations, shuffle action labels within each session (preserving session structure and url_before url_after pairing), recompute per-stratum PMI, take weighted mean across strata. The null mean must satisfy |mean| < 0.1 bits for any estimator to pass C1. Unit of permutation is action-label within session (same as parent).
measurement_validity: SPA uses the same 12-state hash-routed design as parent with CANDIDATES guaranteeing all (state, action) pairs have 4 distinct next states.
Determinism check: for every (state, action) pair, |unique(CANDIDATES[state][action])| >= 2. If any pair fails, the experiment is MEASUREMENT_INVALID.
N=5000 transitions (50 sessions x 100 steps) with seed=42, same collection procedure as parent.
Strata with < 5 records are skipped (MIN_STRATUM_SIZE=5, same as parent).
All estimators use Laplace smoothing alpha=1.0 for comparability with parent.
Bootstrap CI uses 200 trajectory-block resamples (same as parent).
Bonferroni correction for 7 primary comparisons (4 parent + 3 orthogonal): alpha=0.00714.

Orthogonal estimators implemented as follows: KSG CMI via sklearn.feature_selection.mutual_info_classif with k=5; Bayesian via pymc Dirichlet-Multinomial with variational inference; likelihood-ratio via scipy.stats.chi2_contingency with Bonferroni correction.
If any orthogonal estimator fails due to implementation issues, report the failure as MEASUREMENT_INVALID with explicit error message.
decision_rule:
Verdict priority: FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING > MEASUREMENT_INVALID > SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST.

FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING triggers if ANY of:
  (1) C1: All 7 estimators have |shuffled-action null mean| >= 0.1 bits at N=5000
  (2) C3: For any estimator passing C1, positive control K3 < 1.0 bit OR p > 0.001
  (3) Determinism check fails (any (state,action) has < 2 unique candidates)

MEASUREMENT_INVALID triggers if:
  (4) Fewer than 30% of (state,action) strata have >= 5 records at N=5000
  (5) stratum_size_bias_decomposition has < 2 non-empty size buckets
  (6) Any orthogonal estimator implementation fails (e.g., missing dependency, convergence error)

SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST requires ALL of:
  (C1) At least 1 estimator (parent or orthogonal) has |null_mean| < 0.1 bits
  (C3) Positive control passes for that estimator
  (C6) Determinism check passes
  (C7) >= 2 non-empty size buckets in stratum decomposition

Phase 2 (beyond-Markov, only if SURVIVES on C1):
  (C2) K3 PMI - K2 PMI > 0.1 bits AND bootstrap 95% CI lower > 0.0
  (C4) |K2(N=50000) - K2(N=5000)| <= 0.2 bits for the best estimator
product_consequence_positive: If bias eliminated (H1 passes): the PMI research program is unblocked. Valid beyond-Markov testing becomes possible on this SPA class. The estimator bias problem is resolved by switching to orthogonal frameworks, not by SPA redesign. This opens the path to: (a) testing K3-K2 on the stochastic SPA, (b) re-validating prior parent signals (0.933-bit K2 PMI) with proper null centering, (c) eventually testing on production SPAs with stochastic transitions.
product_consequence_negative: If bias persists (H0 confirmed): the plug-in PMI estimator and its orthogonal variants are fundamentally biased for strata-varying-size SPA estimation. This closes the orthogonal-estimator pathway and requires pivoting to fundamentally different detection paradigms (entropy rate, channel capacity, causal discovery) or abandoning synthetic SPA simulation for production Web data with alternative state representations and estimators.
estimated_cost: Low-medium. Single Python script execution on 12-state SPA, N=5000 primary + N=50000 convergence test. ~15 minutes compute (including Bayesian variational inference). 500 shuffled-action permutations. No browser/network required. Uses existing parent run_experiment.py infrastructure with added orthogonal estimator implementations.
expected_information_gain: High. This experiment answers the critical fork question from the parent handoff: can orthogonal estimators eliminate the plug-in PMI null bias? A definitive answer in either direction closes one pathway and opens the other. The experiment is small but resolves the highest-uncertainty question in the Physics lane's current state.
